matched_nothing: No rows matched in {table} — nothing changed
confirm_destructive_warning: ⚠️  Warning: DELETE operation is destructive and cannot be undone!
confirm_destructive_prompt: Are you sure you want to execute this DELETE operation? This cannot be undone.
confirm_destructive_warning_ddl: ⚠️  Warning: this schema change is destructive and cannot be undone!
confirm_ddl_prompt: Are you sure you want to run this {operation}? This cannot be undone.
gate_full_table_warning: ⚠️  This affects EVERY row in {table} and cannot be undone.
gate_ddl_warning: ⚠️  This destroys {table} and cannot be undone.
gate_ddl_warning_untargeted: ⚠️  This is a destructive schema change and cannot be undone.
gate_unparseable_warning: ⚠️  dbcli could not parse this statement, so it is treated as affecting everything.
gate_multiple_statements_warning: ⚠️  This is more than one statement, and dbcli will not judge them one at a time.
gate_multi_table_warning: This write joins another table. How many rows of the target it touches depends on the data, not on the statement, so it cannot be checked before it runs.
gate_nested_write_warning: ⚠️  This statement carries a second write inside it, and dbcli will not read the tier of that write off this one.
gate_typed_mismatch: That did not match {phrase}. Nothing was run.
gate_refused: Refused: this statement is not limited to specific rows and nobody is here to confirm it (reason={reason}).
gate_refused_in_shell: Refused: a dbcli subcommand started from the shell has no way to ask you, even though you are right here (reason={reason}).
gate_remedy_no_where: Add a WHERE clause — WHERE 1=1 if you really do mean every row — or a LIMIT, then run it again.
gate_remedy_ddl_destruction: No flag skips this. Run it from an interactive terminal, or apply the schema change through a reviewed migration.
gate_remedy_unparseable: dbcli could not parse this statement and will not guess. Simplify it, or run it from an interactive terminal.
gate_remedy_multi_table: Rewrite it as a single-table statement — move the other table into a subquery in the WHERE — or run it where someone can confirm it.
gate_remedy_nested_write: Run the nested write as its own statement, or run this one where someone can confirm it.
gate_remedy_non_unique_where: Match on a primary key or a uniquely indexed column, or run it from an interactive terminal.
gate_remedy_in_shell: Type the statement at the dbcli> prompt instead — there the shell asks you to type the target table name.
recovery_none: This cannot be undone automatically — restore from a backup to get the previous values back.
recovery_retry: Re-run with --recovery to write a recovery plan, then read it with: dbcli recover
blacklist_hint: Run `dbcli blacklist list` to see what is protected
